title: Om as Its Measures
meter: Prose (the Upaniṣad mantras have no meter)
meterNote: The mantras of the Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad are prose, not verse, so there is no meter to scan. Their rhythm comes from the chant. Notice how this mantra uses pāda and mātrā, the same two words the meter scanner is built on.
translation: This Self, seen as a syllable, is Om; seen as measures: the quarters are the measures and the measures are the quarters, namely A, U and M.
translation_hi: यह आत्मा अक्षर की दृष्टि से ओंकार है, और मात्राओं की दृष्टि से: पाद ही मात्राएँ हैं और मात्राएँ ही पाद हैं, अर्थात् अकार, उकार और मकार।

words.note: Also: the mātrās (morae) the meter scanner counts!

grammar: Pāda and mātrā: the Upaniṣad maps the four quarters of the Self onto the measures of Om, using the exact words Sanskrit prosody uses for a verse's quarters and its syllable lengths.
-kāra 'sound': अकार, उकार, मकार; Om itself is ओङ्कार, 'the Om-sound'.
Om = A + U + M: in sandhi, अ + उ → ओ (guṇa), then म्: अ-उ-म् → ओम्.
